mutations.because: Carry source BACK on undo instead of forward (R5): the revision the server just handed back rewinds to the pre-save value, and the next conditional save If-Matches a revision that no longer exists — the undo itself creates the conflict the carry rule exists to prevent.
command: leaves source.revision unchanged by the undo

mutations.because: Leave the stacks intact after a baseline replace: undoing a load/discard/restore walks back into a draft that no longer exists — the stored-draft restore would offer an undo over state the user never had in this session.
command: replaces the baseline and clears undo AND redo

mutations.because: Make save undoable: the save receipt is a server answer (R4), and an undo step over it would present a draft revert that also implies an unsent write — the revision guard then lies about what has been saved. (Re-anchored by ANCHORS: the recorded text was reformatted or moved, not changed — the after-text is re-wrapped the same way, and the edit it encodes, the claim and the command are untouched. Re-anchored again, PT-5c1 fix round: the array gained a fifth member, "markSeeded" (also a server answer, never a draft edit) — same claim about "save" specifically, same test, only the array's own text moved.)
command: save alone creates no undo step

mutations.before: const coalesced = key !== null && key === history.lastKey;
mutations.because: Turn coalescing off: every keystroke becomes its own history entry, so undoing 'a word' takes a hundred presses and the acceptance criterion 'typing a word is one undo step' is what breaks first.
command: typing a word is one undo step

mutations.because: Move setPool to the non-undoable side of the line: the lane's stated decision is that setPool IS a draft edit (it writes variation.headline), and an undo that could not step back over the dropped headline is the observable half of that decision. (Re-anchored by ANCHORS: the recorded text was reformatted or moved, not changed — the mutation, its claim and its command are untouched.)

Drop the keyboard wiring in the component that owns it: the hook can be perfectly correct and the user still has no ⌘Z — the editor-level suite pins the chord through the real page, not just the hook.
command: VE1 — undo and redo in the editor

mutations.because: Purge on EVERY pristine render, not only on a return to pristine: mount starts pristine, and this session never diverged from it, so a stored draft whose visible content matches the blank editor is DELETEd on that very render — before the restore effect (a separate, async effect) ever gets to read it. The gate this mutation drops is what makes the delete a same-session-divergence-only action; without it, the mount's own pristine render is indistinguishable from a genuine return to pristine. Re-anchored for PT-5d: the storage calls became putServerDraft/deleteServerDraft and the branch order flipped (still-diverging first, pristine second), but the divergedRef gate this mutation strips is unchanged.
command: a draft stored before mount is still offered for restore on mount

mutations.because: Drop the return-to-pristine purge (the finding as reported): the autosave effect still never removes a stored draft, so an undone brief comes back after reload — with undo one keystroke away, returning to exactly pristine is easy, and the stale draft arrives with no history left to undo it. Re-anchored for PT-5d, then again for the bot fix round: `deleteServerDraft` replaces `purgeDraftFromStorage`, and the write now goes through `enqueueDraftWrite` (the client-side write chain) instead of a bare call, but the branch this mutation deletes — the return-to-pristine cleanup itself — is the same one.
command: undoing back to pristine purges the autosaved draft

mutations.because: Remove the modal-dialog guard from the chord handler: with a dialog open and focus on one of its buttons, ⌘Z reaches through the scrim and edits the brief behind it — the second reported bug, invisible to the typing-target check that was the only deferral before.
command: ⌘Z from a control inside an open modal dialog is left alone

mutations.because: While a modal is open the page behind it is inert: the history shortcut must be ignored whenever an aria-modal element is in the document, not only when the chord lands inside it. A target-only check let ⌘Z on the document body (focus after a scrim click) undo the draft behind an open Save-as dialog.
